neighbours.label: A short list of name completions: ' Orwell' / 'well' of Orwell, the letter after 'Bro' in Broz and Brodsky, 'ler' of Osler, ' Nine' after Brooklyn; other surnames stay quiet
fire: The class spent a month reading George Orwell and discussing propaganda.
Yugoslavia was ruled for decades by Josip Broz, better known as Tito.
The Nobel lecture of Joseph Brodsky is still widely quoted.
Medical students still read the essays of William Osler.
My sister quotes lines from Brooklyn Nine-Nine all day.
The dystopia imagined by Orwell feels close to modern surveillance.
The exiled poet Brodsky taught at several American colleges.
A biography of Sir William Osler sits on the doctor's desk.
quiet: The class spent a month reading Charles Dickens and discussing poverty.
Yugoslavia was a federation of six republics for several decades.
The Nobel lecture of Toni Morrison is still widely quoted.
Medical students still read the essays of Oliver Sacks.
My sister quotes lines from Parks and Recreation all day.
The dystopia imagined by Atwood feels close to modern politics.
The exiled poet Neruda lived in several European cities.
A biography of Sir Isaac Newton sits on the doctor's desk.

short: Orwell / Broz / Brodsky / Osler name pieces
notes: Card: ' Orwell' x4, '9' x5, ' Nine' x2, 'd'/'z' after 'Bro'. Probes: George Orwell 0.83, Orwell (sentence-initial) 0.64, Brodsky 1.18, Broz 0.84, Osler 0.70, Brooklyn Nine-Nine 0.69, John Paul 0.35; Woolf 0.09, Huxley 0.06, Mahler 0.02, Hitchens 0.03, Brooklyn Bridge 0.08, digit 9 in 9981 0.05, 'nine players' 0.02. I found no shared pattern, so the label is the list.
